title: The Playlist of Cedar Falls
premise: Orsen Underhill has spent twelve years being invisible at Cedar Falls High, a school built over the flooded ruins of the town's first settlement. When a group chat called The Playlist begins sending song titles that predict disasters hours before they happen, Orsen discovers he can hear the songs before anyone sends them — because the drowned town beneath the school is choosing him as its voice. As predictions turn from pranks to deaths, Orsen must win the state swim championship to keep the school open (and the seal over the old town intact) while secretly racing to give the forgotten dead the memorial they were denied. In the end, Orsen chooses memory over power: he breaks the seal by singing the town's true name aloud, flooding the championship and his own careful anonymity, but freeing both towns — the living one above and the remembered one below.
about_author: Freya Crane grew up in a river town where the high school parking lot was rumored to cover an old cemetery, an idea that never quite left her. She writes young adult fiction about quiet kids who discover the past has been listening all along.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On his first day as a junior, Orsen maps every exit, every social risk, every way to remain unseen — a habit born from a childhood accident he refuses to remember. When he hears faint music coming up through the gym floor during swim practice, he tells no one. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A chat invitation appears on his phone for 'The Playlist,' six members he half-knows, discussing a fire in the chemistry lab — which happens forty minutes later. Orsen realizes he received the message before it was sent. Emotional beat: vertigo, the collapse of his carefully ordered world.

chapters.title: Six Strangers and a Song
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third POV among the chat members: Priya the skeptic, Dez the prankster, Marisol the archivist's daughter, twins Wren and Theo, and quiet Jonah. They compare timestamps and realize the predictions are real. Emotional beat: wary excitement of shared secret-keeping.

chapters.title: What the Gym Is Standing On
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She shows the group her mother's archive: Cedar Falls High was built in 1961 over Old Cedar Falls, drowned when the reservoir was made, its residents relocated and its name struck from records. The first predicted song was a hymn from the old town's church. Emotional beat: history as something buried but breathing.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Predicted
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The Playlist predicts a balcony collapse at homecoming. The group debates warning people; Dez posts anonymously, gets mocked, and the balcony groans anyway — held up only because Orsen, hearing the hymn swell, physically braces it. Emotional beat: the cost of being believed too late.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Hears First
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Orsen: the messages originate near him, timestamped seconds before sending. Orsen denies it, terrified, but that night the music follows him home through the drains. Emotional beat: fear of being the anomaly, the chosen one.

chapters.title: Coach Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Swim coach Voss reveals she knows about the old town — her grandmother refused evacuation and drowned singing. She tells Orsen the district plans to demolish and rebuild the school, which will break whatever holds the memories down. The championship meet decides the school's funding. Emotional beat: duty arriving disguised as sport.

chapters.title: Setlist for a Drowning
chapters.summary: Marisol and Orsen's dual POV. Decoding the playlist order, they find it mirrors the old town's church service — building toward a final hymn that, per archive marginalia, was sung 'to call everyone home.' The next prediction is a name: Underhill. Emotional beat: dread turning personal.

chapters.title: Jonah Stops Talking
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. After the playlist predicts 'a silence,' Jonah loses his voice entirely — taken as payment. The group realizes each fulfilled prediction costs someone something. Guilt fractures their unity. Emotional beat: the price of curiosity.

chapters.title: Rivalry Meets Ruin
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the away meet against Ashgrove, Orsen swims the race of his life while hearing the hymn under the water itself. He wins, but the pool drains mysteriously overnight, and the playlist updates: 'the water remembers where it lived.' Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by inevitability.

chapters.title: Priya Breaks the Rules
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Convinced it's a hoax with deadly consequences, Priya leaks the chat to the principal. The school locks down, searches phones, and suspends Dez. That night the playlist predicts Priya's own house flood — and it happens exactly as warned. Emotional beat: skepticism shattered into belief.

chapters.title: Under the Floorboards of Fourth Period
chapters.summary: Orsen and Wren's dual POV. Following the music through maintenance tunnels, they find the sealed foundation: a preserved street, lampposts, a church door — and twelve years of Orsen's lost memories playing on the walls like film. His childhood accident happened here; the town saved him then. It wants acknowledgment now. Emotional beat: memory as debt.

chapters.title: The One That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Training montage of the soul: Voss pushes Orsen toward the championship while the town's fate hangs elsewhere. Orsen realizes the swim title is the distraction — the real contest is whether anyone will remember Old Cedar Falls before demolition day. Emotional beat: learning which fights are real.

chapters.title: Marisol's Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The historical archive catches fire — predicted by the playlist as 'ash and amen' — destroying the records that could restore the old town's legal existence. Marisol saves one ledger: the original church register with every resident's name. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Twins Divide
chapters.summary: Wren and Theo's alternating POV. Theo wants to use the playlist's power — predict lottery numbers, games, futures — and discovers he can feed it desires in exchange for small miracles. Wren watches her brother's eyes go reservoir-calm and cold. Emotional beat: power's seduction inside a family.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The district moves the rebuild date up: demolition in nine days, right after championships. The playlist goes silent — the worst sign yet. Jonah writes on paper: 'It's done asking.' The group reunites around a single plan. Emotional beat: unity forged by deadline.

chapters.title: What Theo Bought
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Theo's traded wishes unravel: his winnings vanish, his luck inverts, and the playlist claims him as 'the second voice.' He begins speaking in the old town's dialect without knowing it. Orsen realizes the town doesn't want worship — it wants to be finished, laid properly to rest. Emotional beat: horror of corruption by gift.

chapters.title: Championship Eve
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The night before the meet, the reservoir level drops impossibly, and the whole town hears the hymn. Voss gives Orsen her grandmother's hymnal. The playlist sends one final prediction, addressed to Orsen alone: 'Tomorrow you sing, or tomorrow we rise.' Emotional beat: calm before total commitment.

chapters.title: The Race Above, The Name Below
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax part one. Mid-championship-final, the pool splits open onto the drowned street. Officials evacuate; Orsen dives instead, swimming down through the hymn into the church, where the register waits on the altar. Emotional beat: choosing the impossible dive.

chapters.title: Every Name Aloud
chapters.summary: Orsen and ensemble POV, climax part two. In the flooded church, Orsen reads the register — every resident's name — while the group above holds back Theo, who begs the town to take him as its voice instead. The hymn resolves; the water stills; the dead step out of memory, nod once, and let go. Emotional beat: remembrance as release, not power.

chapters.title: After the Water Settles
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The school stands damaged but saved; the reservoir refills gentle and quiet. Jonah's voice returns mid-sentence. Theo, hollowed but human, turns himself toward repair. The town votes to build the new school beside — not over — a memorial bearing 214 names. Emotional beat: grief integrated, community rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Last Track
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, coda. Months later, Orsen swims in the new pool and hears nothing beneath him except water. But on graduation day, his phone buzzes once: a single message from The Playlist — a song title he doesn't recognize, and a date far in the future. He smiles, saves it, and finally stops being careful. Emotional beat: belonging, and the courage to be known.
